Marta (ACME): hey team — starting ~09:15 PST our nightly rerank job is getting 429s from the /v1/rerank endpoint. generation and embeddings endpoints are fine. This started suddenly and only affects rerank traffic. sample response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` with headers `X-RateLimit-Limit: 120`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 28`, `x-org-quota-remaining: 40000`. job id: acme-rerank-20260314-09. We haven't changed client config. Any fast ideas?

Priya (Support): thanks Marta. can you paste the exact curl (sanitized token ok) + the approximate requests/sec and requests/minute you saw? also which API key/org did the job use? sounds like an endpoint-specific quota but need details to confirm.

Marta (ACME): here's a sanitized repro:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"queries":["Which product is best?","..."],"candidates":[["p1","p2",... 256 candidates ...],[...]],"top_k":5}'
```
We normally send 10 queries per request, each with ~256 candidates. Normal throughput: ~500 req/min. At 09:12 we saw a sudden retry storm (client retries kicking in) and at peak ~1.2k req/min.

Jamal (Support): copying @Eli (SRE) for quota view. Marta — did your client do immediate retries or exponential backoff? any change in batching recently?

Marta (ACME): our in-house client retries 3x with no jitter (0ms -> 500ms -> 1000ms). no recent batching changes.

rate-limit-bot: detected: org=acme-org endpoint=/v1/rerank bucket=rerank.default window=60s limit=120 used=121 remaining=0 reset_in=18s

Eli (SRE): quick findings: rerank traffic is counted against a separate endpoint quota (rerank.default) with a per-org/min window. ACME is hitting that bucket because they do many small requests with large candidate arrays. Two contributors: 1) client-side immediate retries (no jitter) that amplify transient 429s, 2) per-endpoint quota for rerank is lower than scoring/embeddings. We also saw many short bursts from the same API key across multiple worker instances (thundering herd).

Eli (SRE): recommended immediate steps: (a) implement exponential backoff with jitter on client (b) reduce freq: batch more queries per request if possible (we suggest <=64 candidates per query where feasible) (c) we can do a temporary quota bump for acme-org while you deploy client fixes. I can action the bump if you confirm org id.

Priya (Support): ACTIONS NEEDED FROM CUSTOMER: please test a small change to client backoff. Quick test command to reproduce locally (safe load):
```bash
# run a controlled load (10 qps) to validate backoff behavior
for i in {1..60}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -d '{"queries":["q"],"candidates":[["a","b","c"]]}' &
  sleep 0.1
done
```
Then compare "429" counts with/without backoff.

Marta (ACME): ran test after flipping client to exponential backoff + jitter (base 200ms, max 2s). result: 429s dropped to zero in our test window. thanks. Can you do the temporary increase while we roll client?

Eli (SRE): confirmed — we increased rerank.default quota for acme-org from 120/min -> 600/min for 4 hours (temporary). rate-limit-bot recorded: quota_update org=acme-org bucket=rerank.default old=120 new=600 reason="support-bump for rollout" expires_in=14400s

Jamal (Support): summary & next steps: 1) we applied a temporary quota bump (Eli) 2) customer to roll client backoff & batching change (Marta) 3) Support to submit formal quota increase request to Product (we'll need expected sustained rps + peak) 4) Recommend long-term: treat rerank traffic as part of shared scoring quota or provide a rerank-specific committed plan for high-volume customers — assigned to @Priya to own comms.

Marta (ACME): appreciated. we'll limit candidates to 64 per query and gate workers to 2 reqs/sec per instance until formal quota increase approved. please send confirmation email of the quota bump & expiration so our on-call is aware. :thumbsup:

Priya (Support): sending email now, and opening a ticket with product for the quota bump path. tagging @Eli for a short follow-up: can we add a per-key header in responses so clients can more easily detect which bucket they hit? current headers show X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining but don't include bucket name.

Eli (SRE): noted. I'll file an internal request to add X-RateLimit-Bucket header and include it in debug logs. low-risk change but requires a small runtime change.

rate-limit-bot: event=quota_bump applied org=acme-org bucket=rerank.default new_limit=600 expires=2026-03-14T13:12:36Z by=eli.sre

Jamal (Support): closing loop for now — docing incident in support tracker and will produce a short post-incident checklist for customers who run large rerank workloads (client backoff, batching recommendations, per-key monitoring). Will follow up with timeline for permanent quota change.

Marta (ACME): great, thanks everyone — we'll monitor and report if anything else crops up.

[thread end]
